newsitem.title: JAPAN: Honda to launch new compact car in Japan.
newsitem.headline: Honda to launch new compact car in Japan.

text.p: Honda Motor Co Ltd said on Thursday that it would launch a new "Logo" compact three- and five-door hatchback car which will be cheaper than similar cars made by its rivals.

The company announced at a press preview that it would start selling the three-door Logo on Friday, and launch the five-door version on November 1, and aim for a total monthly sales target of 6,000 units.
"The Logo is competitively priced against other Japanese makers' compact cars," Michiyoshi Hagino, a Honda managing director, told Reuters.

Other makers' cars of a similar class with similar equipment are priced at around 1.05 to 1.06 million yen, but the domestic selling price of Logo will range from 770,000 to 1.088 million yen, he said.

"This car is in the 1.0- to 1.3-litre class. This market now stands at about 300,000 units per year and is expected to expand because of an increase in the number of elderly and female drivers," said Riku Iwai, a Honda managing director.
Honda has no plans to export the Logo model, Iwai said.
In producing the Logo, Honda will use Chinese-made components in its Japanese-made cars for the first time.

The Logo will use camshafts made by Dong Feng Honda Auto Parts Co Ltd in Huizhou, Guangdong province, which is a 50-50 venture between Honda and the Dong Feng Group, an automaker based in Shiyan, another Honda official said.
The camshafts made by Dong Feng Honda will be used for half of the projected monthly sales of 6,000 units, he said.
Honda will use Dong Feng-made brake discs and brake drums in Logo models from next year, he said.
"After launching the Logo model, we plan to launch two new models in Japan, aimed at young people, in the near future," said Honda president Nobuhiko Kawamoto.
